metadata.title: Azure SQL Database - SC-28 / SC-28(1) Component Definition
metadata.remarks: Platform-specific layer (3b). Describes how an Azure SQL Database meets SC-28 and SC-28(1) and which technology-agnostic rules verify it. The rules and their checks are defined once, in the imported datastore-checks component definition (3a); this file only references their Rule_Ids. Organisation parameter values live in the organisation profile (2b, the source below); the selection for sc-28_odp.01 and system-specific values live in the SSP. The Azure adapter (automation/azure_arm_inventory.py) maps this component's settings onto the datastore inventory that the checks read.

components.title: Azure SQL Database
components.description: Azure SQL logical server and database. Data at rest (data files, transaction logs and backups) is encrypted with Transparent Data Encryption (TDE), which is enabled by default for new databases. A database created as a ledger database (isLedgerOn) additionally SHA-256 hashes every change into a Merkle-tree blockchain whose digests are stored outside the database, making tampering detectable; ledger can only be set when the database is created.

control-implementations.description: SC-28 and SC-28(1) implementation for Azure SQL Database data at rest, against the organisation profile.

implemented-requirements.description: Confidentiality of data at rest: Transparent Data Encryption (verified by datastore_encrypted_at_rest). Integrity of data at rest: ledger tamper evidence (verified by datastore_tamper_evident), which requires the database to be created with isLedgerOn = true.

sc-28.1_obj-1 (disclosure): TDE performs real-time AES-256 encryption and decryption of the data files, transaction logs and backups, so stored data is not disclosed if storage or backup media are accessed outside SQL Server (datastore_encrypted_at_rest). sc-28.1_obj-2 (modification): a ledger database SHA-256 hashes every change into a Merkle-tree blockchain with digests stored outside the database, so unauthorized modification, including by privileged users, is detected when the ledger is verified (datastore_tamper_evident). This is the cryptographic tamper evidence accepted by the organisation guidance; it detects rather than prevents modification.

components.remarks: Datastore inventory mapping used by the Azure adapter: encryption_at_rest.enabled is true unless a Microsoft.Sql/servers/databases/transparentDataEncryption resource sets properties.state = Disabled (TDE is on by default); tamper_evidence.enabled is true only if the Microsoft.Sql/servers/databases resource sets properties.isLedgerOn = true (off by default, fixed at creation).
